html:
The royal drums of Burundi are large drums once kept at royal sanctuaries and played at the rituals of the Burundian monarchy, now played by drum groups in a dance listed by UNESCO in 2014.

The great drum stood for the king himself, and the word for drum, ingoma, also meant kingdom. Teams of drummers played in rotation, with dancers leaping before them, at royal rites such as Umuganuro, the sowing festival.

Recordings of Burundian drummers made in the 1960s were sampled in a 1971 hit, Burundi Black, and their beat was taken up by British pop bands in the 1980s. The drums outlived the monarchy and are played at national events across Burundi, linking the country to its past.
sum: The royal drums of Burundi are large drums once kept at royal sanctuaries and played at the rituals of the Burundian monarchy, now played by drum groups in a dance listed by UNESCO in 2014.
